summary: Alexandr Wang describes a model that was co-trained together with its agent, reporting higher first-attempt tool-call success, cleaner plan execution and less re-prompting, with a 1 million token context window, illustrated by a kernel-optimization run of over 1,000 tool calls.

mechanisms.reason: A stated 1M token context window increases KV-cache and memory footprint per served request.

practices.reason: Co-training model and agent is claimed to improve tool-call success and reduce re-prompting, but no quantified benchmark is given, only a qualitative claim and one long-context figure.
practices.quote: we co-trained the model and agent together. the result: higher first-attempt success on tool calls, cleaner plan execution, less time re-prompting. 1m token context window.

practices.reason: An informal stress-test (kernel optimization run with 1,000+ tool calls) is described as an example demonstration rather than a transferable eval methodology.
practices.quote: we pointed it at kernel optimization on nvidia hopper and let it run. 1,000+ tool calls
